newsitem.title: UK: Cinven buys health interests from Gen. des Eaux. [CORRECTED 11:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cinven buys health interests from Gen. des Eaux. [CORRECTED 11:10 GMT]

text.p: British fund management firm Cinven Ltd said on Wednesday it had bought the health activities of French conglomerate Generale des Eaux in a deal valued at 1.1 billion pounds ($1.8 billion).

Cinven is organising what it called the largest European management buyout of the decade, which will see the managements of General des Eaux's two businesses Generale de Sante in France and General Healthcare Group in the UK run the businesses as separate and independent companies by their respective management teams. (Corrects to make clear that Cinven owns the businesses.)

"The European private healthcare market offers significant opportunities for expansion and we will provide the investment backing necessary to take advantage of the increasing market for private healthcare and hospital facilities and resources," said Simon Rowlands, a director at Cinven.
Generale des Eaux announced in April it was considering two offers for its health business, one from Cinven and the other from fund manager BC Partners.
Cinven also said it planned to merge hospital provider Amicus Healthcare, which it owns, with General Healthcare.
Under the terms of the deal, Generale des Eaux will retain a 20 percent stake in Paris-based Generale de Sante.
